title: Flat representatives for etale pullback, finite twists and shifts
statement: Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$, separated finite-type $k$-schemes $T,T'$, and a $k$-morphism $u:T'\to T$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $N=\ell^n\ge1$ and let $R$ be a finite commutative ring with $NR=0$. Use ordinary small-etale constant-ring module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], exact module inverse image $u^*$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], constructibility [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], and Tor amplitude [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Define $R_{T'}(1)=\mu_{N,T'}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_{T'}}R_{T'}$ and $R_{T'}(c)=R_{T'}(1)^{\otimes c}$ for $c\ge0$, with $R_{T'}(0)=R_{T'}$, as in [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line]. Let $a\le b$, let $K$ be bounded constructible of Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ on $T$, and let $P$ be any representing cochain complex of flat constructible $R_T$-modules zero outside $[a,b]$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. For every $c\ge0$ and $s\in\mathbf Z$, the complex $(u^*P\otimes_{R_{T'}}R_{T'}(c))[s]$ is a K-flat representative [def-pc-kflat-complex] of $(u^*K\otimes^L_{R_{T'}}R_{T'}(c))[s]$, with flat constructible terms and zero terms outside $[a-s,b-s]$. Consequently this derived object is bounded constructible of Tor amplitude in $[a-s,b-s]$; in particular $u^*$ itself preserves $[a,b]$.

proof.text: The field $k$ is Noetherian: every ideal is either $(0)$ or $(1)$. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian, using its single affine chart and its one-point underlying space. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to the finite-type structure morphisms $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $T\prime\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Both $T$ and $T\prime$ are Noetherian, so the scheme hypotheses of the termwise model theorem and the flat-model existence theorem used below hold.

Since $\ell\ne p$ and both are prime, the integer $N=\ell^n$ has nonzero image in $k$, also when $n=0$. Its inverse in $k$ maps to an inverse in every local ring of $T\prime$. Apply [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line] with scheme $T\prime$, coefficient ring $A=R$ and exponent $r=c$. The assumptions $N\ge1$ and $NR=0$ are exactly those in the item. For $E=R_{T\prime}(c)$ this gives an etale covering trivializing $E$ as the constant $R$-module sheaf of rank one, including $c=0$. This verifies the line hypothesis of the existing termwise model theorem; no assumption that $R$ is flat over $\mathbf Z/N$ is used.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-etale-pullback-line-flat-model] to the prescribed complex P, its representing isomorphism, f, the finite Tate line and the shift s. Convert the line cover from the localized small-etale site to the small-etale site of each covering scheme using overSheafEquivFunctorObjOverIso and constantSheafSheafCongrIso. The theorem gives flat constructible terms, support [a-s,b-s], K-flatness, invertibility of the canonical representative comparison, constructible cohomology and Tor amplitude of the localized model. Invert that comparison. The existing derived tensor commShiftIso (the localization of the coherent signed tensor shift structure [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts]) moves the shift of the second factor to the shift of the whole tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]. The composition is the required representing isomorphism. The termwise composition of the two functors is definitionally the specified pullbackTwistComplex.

proof.text: Transport the model Tor amplitude to the represented object using hasTorAmplitudeIn_iff_torAmplitudeIn and invariance under isomorphism. Testing against the monoidal unit gives cohomology concentrated in [a-s,b-s], hence boundedness. Transport constructibility of the model cohomology using the localization homologyFunctorFactors isomorphism and the representing isomorphism. The equivalence of finite-value and finite-stalk constructibility allows use of the existing isomorphism invariance theorem. This establishes precisely bounded constructibility and [def-kun-tor-amplitude].

proof.text: For arbitrary bounded constructible K of Tor amplitude [a,b], apply [lem-sf-etale-flat-constructible] directly to obtain a flat constructible representative P supported in [a,b]; no change of coefficients is needed. Apply the same arbitrary-line model argument with c=0 and s=0. The zeroth finite Tate twist is the actual constant coefficient sheaf, which is the sheaf tensor unit. Compose the representing isomorphism with the zero-shift isomorphism, singleFunctorObjUnitIso, and the derived right unitor. Transport constructibility and Tor amplitude as in the preceding step. Since a-0=a and b-0=b, this proves the final clause with unchanged endpoints.
